title: Design System: BBC — the Bull Broadcasting Corporation

display.purpose: The one hero headline per surface. Source Serif 4 at ~16ch measure, set almost solid.

headline.purpose: The headline inside a lower third and section-opening statements. Text-balanced.

title.purpose: The figure in a Stat, the yes-price in a rundown row, the heading of an empty state. Always paired with .numeric when numeric.

strapline.purpose: The second line under a lower third, and the text of a breaking cut-in. Archivo 600 at sentence length.

body.purpose: Explanatory prose at a 52-70ch measure. Plain Archivo, normal weight.

label.purpose: Every small label without exception: section names, pills, button text, table headers, statuses, tape tags, nav items, timestamps.

shadows.name: monitor
shadows.purpose: The single structural shadow in the system. The pool beneath a lit studio monitor panel. Nothing else casts a shadow.

shadows.name: monitor-lit
shadows.purpose: The monitor shadow burning red, paired with a rgba(187,25,25,0.55) border, for the one panel currently on air.

shadows.name: anchor-key
shadows.purpose: The bull anchor's key light against the studio floor, with a blurred red ellipse behind the shoulders.

shadows.name: lamp-pulse
shadows.purpose: The animated expanding ring of the live on-air lamp. Lamps only.

motion.name: ease-broadcast
motion.purpose: The single decelerating ease shared by every animation in the system.

motion.name: cut-in
motion.value: clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0 0 0 0); 620ms; transform-origin: left center
motion.purpose: The signature wipe. How a lower third or a breaking banner arrives on air. Never substitute a fade.

motion.name: cut-up
motion.purpose: Content appearing inside a panel: a new segment row, a settled verification card.

motion.name: roll
motion.value: translate3d(0,0,0) -> translate3d(-50%,0,0); linear infinite; duration from --roll
motion.purpose: The ticker track. Items are duplicated once so the -50% loop is seamless; hover pauses it.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { ticker-track, cut-in, cut-up, lamp { animation: none } }
motion.purpose: All four devices are disabled wholesale. Colour transitions remain.

narrative.overview:
This is a broadcast, not a dashboard. The product is an autonomous prediction-market trader, and the entire interface is built as the 24-hour news channel that covers it — a dark studio, an out-of-focus video wall throwing cold monitor light, a bull anchor camera-right, a red lower third keyed over the bottom of the shot, and a tape rolling along the foot of the screen at all times. The category default for this product is a grid of tiles with an accent colour. This world refuses that outright: the red is not an accent, it is furniture — the bar the headline sits inside, the strap under it, the tag on the tape, the cut-in that interrupts.

The density is a newsroom's: information-dense but ordered by rank, not spread evenly. Big serif headlines carry the story; everything administrative — labels, tags, statuses, buttons, timestamps — collapses into one tiny all-caps tracked Archivo voice, the chyron. That two-voice split does almost all the hierarchy work; there is very little in between. Panels are treated as lit studio monitors rather than paper cards: a slightly lighter face than the studio floor, one hairline bezel, one soft downward shadow, and a 14px corner.

The world is dark by commitment, not by theme toggle. color-scheme: dark is declared at the root and there is no light mode; a broadcast studio is a dark room with lit screens, and BBC red only reads as broadcast red against near-black. Motion is borrowed from vision mixing rather than from web animation: things cut in with a clip-path wipe, they do not fade and scale.
keyCharacteristics: Dark studio ground (#0a0d11) with a light-only, imagery-free video-wall backdrop
BBC broadcast red as page furniture — bars, straps, cut-ins, tape tags
Source Serif 4 headlines against Archivo chyrons, with almost nothing between them
Panels as lit monitors: one bezel, one shadow, 14px corner
Square controls, round lamps: radius is semantic, not decorative
A fixed rolling ticker on every page, occupying the bottom 3.5rem
Every P&L figure visibly labelled as paper

rules.name: The Furniture Rule
rules.body: Red is a surface before it is a colour. If red appears on a screen, it should be filling a bar that carries type — a lower third, a strap, a cut-in, a tape cap, a wordmark box, a button. A stray red border, red icon or red underline is a sign the world has slipped back into accent-colour thinking.

rules.name: The Two-Light Rule
rules.body: The studio is lit by exactly two sources: monitor blue from camera-left and broadcast red from camera-right, both as soft radial gradients at low opacity. Never introduce a third hue into the environment. Status lamps are ink, not light, and do not count.

rules.name: The Paper Label Rule
rules.body: Every P&L, return or performance figure is rendered adjacent to a visible paper-mode marker — an amber hold pill reading 'Paper mode · simulated on Manifold', a 'paper' word in the label itself, or both. A number that could be read as realized cash is a defect, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Type is either a headline (Source Serif) or a chyron (uppercase tracked Archivo). Body prose is the only thing allowed in between, and it is always plain Archivo at a normal weight. There is no third display face, no semibold sans headline, and no serif label.

rules.name: The Chyron Rule
rules.body: If a piece of text is a label rather than a sentence, it takes .chyron — including button text. Sentence-case small text is body copy; if you find yourself wanting a 12px semibold sentence-case label, it is either a chyron or it is prose.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every figure carries .numeric. tnum is on globally at the body, and .numeric sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on top, so prices, percentages, clocks, hashes and P&L columns never jitter as they tick.

rules.name: The Tape Rule
rules.body: A fixed ticker occupies the bottom 3.5rem of every page at z-40. main carries pb-14 to clear it. Nothing critical, and no primary action, may sit in that band.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: Sections are separated by a change of ground (bg-studio-2), a border-rule top edge, or generous vertical padding — never by a floating card with a shadow. The page is a stack of full-width bands the studio light falls across.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Elevation is declared once, by .monitor. Nothing else in the system casts a shadow — not buttons, not pills, not rows, not the header. A second shadow vocabulary means a card has crept in where a monitor belongs.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: The one backdrop-blur in the system is the sticky header (bg-studio/95 backdrop-blur), where it exists so type stays legible over scrolling content. Blur is never used as decoration, and there are no frosted panels.

dos: Do compose the on-air furniture from LowerThird, Ticker, Slug, LiveLamp, StudioClock, AnchorBull and BreakingCutIn rather than building a red bar by hand.
Do put every small label in .chyron — including button text, table headers and statuses — and every figure in .numeric.
Do use newsroom forms for page structure: running orders, rundown rows, transcript columns, straps, tables and the tape.
Do label every P&L figure as paper, with the amber hold pill or the word 'paper' in the label itself.
Do give a panel .monitor (14px, one bezel, one shadow) and let its rows supply their own padding under overflow-hidden.
Do name the action in a control's label ('Put this market on air', 'Pull the wire'), never 'Submit'.
Do ship every state — loading, empty, error, hover, focus-visible, disabled. Empty states are a serif headline plus a short dim sentence plus one primary button, centred in a monitor at px-6 py-16.
Do wrap wide tables in their own overflow-x-auto container and hold the layout down to 375px.
Do take icons from lucide-react at a single stroke weight (2 or 2.5), sized size-3 to size-4.
donts: Don't build page structure from cards of icon-plus-heading-plus-text. That is the category default this world exists to refuse.
Don't use red as a sprinkled accent — no lone red icons, red underlines or red micro-borders. Red fills a bar that carries type.
Don't nest a monitor inside a monitor, or give anything but .monitor a shadow.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a heading. Slug names a segment; it never sits over a headline as a decorative pre-title.
Don't use gradient text, glass-blur decoration, or an image or noise texture in the studio environment — the room is lit by CSS light only.
Don't use emoji or unicode glyphs as icons or as section markers. Icons are lucide SVGs; a section marker that carries no information should simply be absent.
Don't number sections 01 / 02 / 03 unless the sequence itself is the information (the Bull Pool's Hold → Trade → Draw is a legitimate use; a list of unrelated panels is not).
Don't introduce a light theme, a third display face, or a second radius value beyond 14px / 0 / round.
Don't place anything critical in the bottom 3.5rem, and don't remove main's pb-14.
Don't move the font variables off <html>; @theme inline resolves them at :root and every headline silently degrades if they move.
Don't write copy that implies realized cash, and don't write 'Arc', 'EVM', 'viem' or 'Ethereum' — the chain is Solana.
